<!-- pr-reviewer: 0172bb464895d8dcaa910f992ed2f6a04be8c203 -->
Review: clean (safety-tier, read-only; not built by the reviewer).

Checked on head 0172bb46:

1. Post order. A C-stamped path carries `PARAM LiveTool`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares `liveTooling`. Its `liveMove` (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps:697`) refuses a first move that is not a rapid. Then it writes `G00 C`, then `G00 X Z` to the end of that move. `rotary_traverse::judge` reads `first.to` with C at that angle. It also reads `first.from`. This is the posted first move.
2. Premise. The turret starts at its index position. A program that starts low is not covered. The module doc and decision item 2 state this.
3. Frames. The work, the parts and the chuck are read in the part frame, about the radius of the first point. The fixed steel is read exactly on the +X station of the spindle line. This agrees with `verify::c_steel` (+X station half-plane, #486). The live tool is always on that station, and fixed steel does not turn. Thus fixed steel at a different C angle cannot meet the tool. The turret body is not modelled (a known limit of #3077, stated). Both ends of the first move are judged. A hit gives `GenError::Invalid` with the kind label first. A value that is not finite also refuses by name.
4. `mill_post_rotary`: a rotary kind on a mill-turn without a C stamp has no `PARAM LiveTool`. Thus the mill post writes it, and the mill laws apply. This is correct.
5. Stamp word `live-traverse-rotary-3096` only for rotary kinds on a lathe or a mill-turn. No mill stamp changes. The diff changes no file in `examples/`, no golden and no catalog project.
6. Fixtures. The first record at r 2, Z28 is inside the 14 x 14 x 34 box stock. That is a true hazard, so clearance 40 is honest. Each test keeps its pinned asserts. `c_axis_unwind` now asserts the mill-turn refusal by name. It keeps the `RapidInStock` orbit conviction on the mill kind, and it adds a `FirstTraverseLow` assert. No coverage is lost.
7. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code. No check is weaker. `rotary_traverse.rs` has 184 lines.

Notes (not blockers):
- `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs` goes from 399 to 403 lines. That is near the 400-line limit. Split it at the next change.
- No integration test pins a part-frame hit on a chuck for the rotary kind. No test runs the Rotary Offset arm (`generate.rs` ~1766). The stock hit is pinned by the `c_axis_unwind` refusal. A follow-up test at `P7` is optional.
- An unstamped rotary kind on a `Lathe` kind is outside `mill_post_rotary` (only `MillTurn`). This PR does not change that case.

Gate: the readings of the worker in the PR body. Heavy lanes: not run. The cut gate covers them. A P1 stack batch gate follows.

Ready and merge: the coordinator flags head 0172bb464 ready and merges it. Review: the Opus safety-tier review (comment 7060676988, marker on 0172bb464, clean; its test notes are #3123, P7). Gate: the P1 stack batch tier on the merged tree with #3125 (8cf7230cf = main + #3125 + this head, local, Windows): 1027 steps, 0 failed; the light tier is green. The trial merge with the current main is clean. Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
